column1: # THE TIMING ROWS (2026-09-30): what a 10-month moving-average exit does on the record's monthly
# S&P, the record's own reading of `timing_of_monthly` / `timingOfMonthly`. At each month's end the
# rule is in equity for the next month when the total-return level is above the mean of the last
# ten month-end levels, this one included, else out; fully invested before the first decision.
# sma10 decline avoided %    over the declines of 20% or more from the running peak (peak to
#                            trough, one still under way included), the share of each decline's
#                            log fall the rule was out for, averaged over the declines
# sma10 false-exit return %  the index's cumulative return over each FALSE exit -- an out-period
#                            no month of which lies in a decline's peak-to-trough window --
#                            averaged over the false exits
# sma10 exits per year       the out-periods (maximal runs of months out) a year
# Graded by where the record falls among the world's single histories of the timing window's
# length (a century), inside the three rows' joint band at 0.05: a one-year block resample keeps
# no decline whole. One ruler for both sets. `Anchors.timing` are this file's records.
# Source, public: Shiller's monthly S&P (http://www.econ.yale.edu/~shiller/data/ie_data.xls, the
# 2023.09 vintage's Data sheet: Date, P, D, CPI), converted to a `month,price,dividend,cpi` CSV;
# the level compounds each month's price ratio with the dividend rate over twelve on the prior
# price, a blank dividend carrying the last one. 1871-01..2023-09, 1833 months, 14 declines.
# Generated by `rust/src/bin/record_bands.rs -timing` (twin: `jsrc/recordBands.sc -timing`):
#   record_bands -timing <data>/shiller-monthly.csv -set sp500 -series Shiller-S&P -header
#   record_bands -timing <data>/shiller-monthly.csv -set nasdaq -series Shiller-S&P
